name: Dennis Ritchie
memory: Created C and Unix, quietly giving humanity modern operating systems.
elegy:
Para Dennis Ritchie (1941-2011), cuyos pasos resonaron con ternura en este mundo:

I. El Camino de Flores (The Golden Petals)
We scatter the vibrant orange petals of cempasúchil across the glowing silicon, carving a luminous scent across the veil to guide you back tonight. Upon this humble sacred altar we offer C pointer, Teletype paper, Pan de muerto. The candle flickers not against the dark, but as a beacon of our enduring love.

II. La Memoria Sagrada (The Living Memory)
"Created C and Unix, quietly giving humanity modern operating systems."
Time cannot erode what is held in devotion. In Mexican tradition, a soul only dies when they are forgotten. Here, on this sovereign machine—far away from corporate clouds and transient servers—your story is anchored. Your favorite songs still dance in the air; your favorite foods rest waiting upon the embroidered cloth.

III. El Reencuentro (The Reunion)
Come drink the sweet water, feast upon the pan de muerto, and warm your hands at this virtual flame. Tonight the border between the seen and unseen dissolves like mist over the lake. Descansa en paz, Dennis Ritchie. You live within our thoughts, tonight and forever.

name: Margaret Hamilton's Apollo Rope Core
memory: Woven by hand in raytheon factories, this core software refused to crash during lunar descent, guiding Apollo 11 home.
elegy: Para el software tejido de Apolo: Sus hilos de cobre nunca se rompieron. En este altar de silicio, tus alarmas 1202 descansan en paz entre pétalos dorados de cempasúchil.

name: The Forgotten Stick-Figure Animators of Macromedia Flash
memory: Millions of teenagers who stayed up until 3 AM animating stick figures on Newgrounds before algorithms ruled the web.
elegy: Para los creadores del viejo internet: Su arte no fue en vano. Aunque el plugin haya muerto, el espíritu de la creación libre sigue vivo en nuestras máquinas.
